## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the 24-hour usage report to include a
"local-turn coverage" section so I can see which sessions actually used the
local LLM, how many turns it answered, what share of the session's turns were
local, and why each session moved to remote — so I can judge whether local is
under-utilised and why.

## Context

The delivered analysis (24h window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52)
showed that 26 of 175 sessions had at least one turn routed to local, and all
225 such turns were answered (100% completion: 214 tool_calls, 10 stop,
1 length). 149 sessions never used local. A proposed section renders this as
three deterministic tables:

1. **Summary table** — rows P10 / P50 / P90 (+ totals) over the sessions with
   ≥1 local turn, columns: # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
   context size at fallback. Sorted by # turns local ascending in the
   percentile rows, more local turns being the goal. Session ID and fallback
   reason are categorical and therefore excluded from the percentile table;
   the reason distribution is provided as its own counts-and-% table (2).
2. **Fallback-reason summary table** — one row per fallback reason with a
   count and a % of the sessions-with-local (P50 # turns local 4.5, # turns
   remote 14.5, % local turns 26.2%; reference-window reason tally below).
3. **Per-session sampling table** — every session with ≥1 local turn,
   columns: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns, reason
   for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns local
   descending (more local = better, best first). 26 rows in the reference
   window. % local turns = local / (local + remote) × 100 per session.

Operational definitions:

- "Routed to local for at least 1 turn and receives a response": a local
  `Stream started` (provider=local) paired with a local `Stream finished`
  (provider=local). All 225 routed turns were answered in the reference
  window; a routed-but-errored turn (Stream finished reason=error) would be
  counted as routed but flagged as unanswered rather than dropped.
- "% local turns": per-session share of turns answered by local
  (local / (local + remote), null when a session has no remote turns →
  100%). Percentiles of this column use linear interpolation like the others.
- "Context size at fallback": `estimated_tokens` from the session's
  `routing_skip_local` line at/near its recorded fallback (remote_move_time),
  falling back to the first remote stream's prompt tokens, and finally to
  start_context_size/max_context_size from the session CSV. Sessions whose
  log lines carry no `tokens=` value render an explicit n/a (3 of 26 in the
  reference window: empty_response / fallback_after_queue sessions) — never a
  fabricated estimate.
- Fallback reason: the session's existing attributed fallback_reason,
  sourced from the session's OWN evidence only (current report contract,
  LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES): own routing_skip_local first, else own
  routing_skip_provider_context, else own Fallback triggered, else — only
  for rotated logs predating the session stamp — the nearest session-less
  fallback line within 60s. Explicit states: `no_remote_fallback`,
  `lease_denied` (local_lease_active refusal), `unattributed` (no own
  evidence). A session's reason is never inherited from an unrelated
  neighbour's global fallback line.

Reference-window fallback-reason tally (26 sessions): rate_limited 11
(42.3%), no remote fallback 4 (15.4%), empty_response 3 (11.5%),
provider_context_exceeded 2 (7.7%), local_concurrency_limit 2 (7.7%), and one
each (3.8%) of HTTP 503, fallback_after_queue, large_context_bypass,
context_too_large.

Notable findings the section should surface as interpretation notes:

- Context-size fallbacks never occur on a session's first message (median
  first-message prompt ~29.6K tokens vs cold_threshold 38000 / warm_threshold
  120000); they fire only after context grows past the thresholds. Reference
  window: 0 of 5268 local-to-remote fallbacks were first-message.
- 96.6% of local-to-remote fallbacks happen before the session has produced
  any local work (routing is decision-first, so local is declined
  pre-emptively, not after a failed attempt).
- rate_limited is the proxy's own per-provider RPM budget pacing
  (provider_budget.py BudgetDecision reason=rate_limited: the configured
  rate_limit_rpm window for that provider entry is exhausted and the request
  is passed through to the next provider immediately), NOT an upstream HTTP
  429 — those surface as upstream_http_error status=429 events instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: report.md contains a deterministic "Local model usage by session"
  section with the summary percentile table (P10/P50/P90 + total row over
  sessions with ≥1 local turn in the window) using the column set: # turns
  local, # turns remote, % local turns, context size at fallback.
- AC2: The section contains the fallback-reason counts-and-% summary table
  (reason, count, % of sessions-with-local).
- AC3: The section contains a per-session table listing each session with ≥1
  local turn: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
  reason for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns
  local descending.
- AC4: Context size at fallback derives from routing_skip_local
  estimated_tokens at/near the session's fallback (falling back to the first
  remote stream's prompt tokens, then session CSV context columns); sessions
  without any token data render "n/a" with a limitation note, never a
  fabricated estimate.
- AC5: The section renders from the existing log/config inputs only (no new
  data sources); the per-session data is present in the session CSVs or an
  explicitly documented new artifact.
- AC6: Rule-based tests cover: session selection (≥1 local turn answered),
  percentile computation (P10/P50/P90, linear interpolation), % local turns
  derivation, fallback attribution (reason + context at fallback), the
  fallback-reason counts-and-% table, sort order, and the no-tokens n/a
  limitation path.
- AC7: The full suite passes via the test skill; the daily 05:00 cron run
  includes the new section with no agent in the loop.

## References

- Reference numbers (window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52): 26/175
  sessions with ≥1 local turn; 225 local turns, 225 answered; P50 local
  turns 4.5, P50 remote turns 14.5, P50 % local turns 26.2%, P50 context at
  fallback ~11K tokens; totals 225 local / 663 remote turns (25.3% local
  overall).
- Skill: .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis (SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md, scripts/).


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25T03:2xZ (plan skill; session herdr-1792897925-2552737-30168):
  pre-check returned `skip` (effort Extra Small, risk Low) — auto-plan path:
  six-stage review only; no child items created.
- Corrected the fallback-reason operational definition to the implemented
  attribution contract (LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES, completed): the prior wording
  ("own routing_skip_first, else nearest Fallback triggered within 60s")
  described the pre-fix attribution that inherited an unrelated neighbour's
  line (11/26 local-using sessions mislabelled as rate_limited in the
  reference window) and contradicted the analysis comment on this item.
- OPEN QUESTION (for implementer / producer): the description's
  reference-window numbers — 26/175 sessions, the fallback-reason tally
  (rate_limited 11, 42.3%; no remote fallback 4, 15.4%; etc.) and the P50
  context-at-fallback figure (~11K tokens) — were computed under the
  pre-fix nearest-line attribution. Recompute the reference numbers from
  real logs under the current attribution contract before finalising the
  section; treat the description's tally as indicative, not authoritative,
  when validating the new section's output.
data.title: Add local-turn coverage report to proxy usage analysis skill

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy maintainer, I want the unused `github` model chain (and its
`github-primary` provider entry) removed from `proxy/config.yaml`, so the
configuration reflects reality and carries no dead routing surface that could
silently attract traffic or confuse future readers.

## Evidence that it is unused

- `proxy/config.yaml` lines ~346-352 declare a `models.github` chain with a
  single remote provider `github-primary` (endpoint
  `https://models.inference.ai.azure.com`, aliases `github-*`).
- Zero traffic in every available proxy log (2026-10-17 14:46 → 2026-10-24
  10:35): no `provider=GitHub`, no `entry=github`, no `github-primary`, no
  `models.inference.ai` occurrences.
- In the 24h usage window (2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52) only three
  initial providers appear across 175 sessions: OpenCode, MunitoAI, and
  local/Qwen3.
- No test in tests/ or proxy/tests/ references the github chain.
- The only other reference is documentation: docs/routing.md:297 notes
  `github-primary` is deliberately ungated (no `model` declared). That note
  must be removed/updated with the chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `github` chain (provider entry `github-primary` and its
  `github-*` aliases) is removed from proxy/config.yaml; no other chain
  references it.
- AC2: The resulting config loads cleanly — proxy startup/config-load tests
  pass, and a config validation/merge test confirms no dangling alias or
  provider reference remains.
- AC3: Documentation is consistent: docs/routing.md no longer describes
  `github-primary` as an ungated provider (remove the paragraph or restate it
  for a surviving ungated entry), and any config header comment naming it is
  updated.
- AC4: A regression test asserts the `github` chain is absent (config-load
  test), so the dead entry cannot be reintroduced unnoticed.
- AC5: If any client is found to request a `github-*` model alias (grep of
  shipped client configs), that must be reported and resolved before removal
  — otherwise AC1/AC4 stand.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill before the change is closed.

## Notes

- The upstream model is unreachable anyway: `github-primary` declares no
  `model`, so the client chooses it; nothing in this deployment exercises
  that path. Removal also drops the "deliberately NOT gated" special case in
  the max_context_tokens documentation block (config.yaml ~line 324).
- Related: model chains shipped after removal are `embed`, `private`, `plan`,
  `author`, `code`, `compact`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and analyst, I want a single per-turn correlation identifier
carried on every structured log line, so a request's full lifecycle — local
routing decision, fallbacks, stream start, stream finish, tokens — can be
reconstructed exactly instead of by FIFO pairing and nearest-line heuristics.

## Why

Today a turn leaves a trail of lines tied together only by session UUID and
timestamp ordering: `routing_skip_local` -> `Fallback triggered` xN ->
`Stream started` -> `Stream finished`. The analysis skill compensates with
heuristics (FIFO stream pairing, 60s fallback windows, nearest-attribution)
that mis-assign reasons (see the rate_limited misattribution in the
2026-10-23/24 window, where a session's own lease denials were overwritten by
an unrelated session's fallback line). A per-request id would remove every
one of these heuristics.

## Design note (plan in implementation)

Emitting an id at the earliest point a request is known (accept/entry) and
carrying it on: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`,
`Fallback triggered`, `routing_hop`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `[local]/[remote]
POST`, `Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`,
`ttft_seconds=`, and the error lines. Short (e.g. 8-hex) to keep lines
readable; both local and remote paths are in different modules
(`proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy_remote.py`), so this is
a cross-cutting change with a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A shared helper (e.g. in `proxy/utils.py` or a new module) generates
  and stamps a per-turn id, and the id is carried on all structured line
  kinds listed above (verify each emit site; no line kind may be left with
  the id unconditionally absent).
- AC2: The id is stable across the full lifecycle of one client request —
  including across fallback hops and chain-hold re-emissions — and unique per
  turn of a session (at minimum within the session).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill consumes the id:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  relevant events; `aggregation.py` pairs streams, fallbacks, skips and TTFT
  events by id (falling back to today's heuristics only when the id is
  absent in older logs); `reporting.py` documents that per-turn attribution is
  exact where ids exist.
- AC4: Skill tests: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` lines with ids; new tests prove
  exact pairing by id (fallback -> stream, skip -> stream, TTFT -> stream)
  and that legacy lines without ids still parse via the existing fallback
  paths.
- AC5: Proxy tests asserting log text are updated where they instantiate or
  assert these lines: `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`.
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`; the pass-through log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` is verified unaffected.
- AC7: Documentation: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` documents the id field and the
  exact-attribution semantics; SKILL.md notes no behavioural change.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill; no regression in the deterministic
  daily report path.

## Notes

- This supersedes most of the pairing heuristics in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`; the change is cross-cutting, so split
  into sub-tasks during planning (shared helper + emit sites; parsers; skill
  consumption; tests) if useful.
- Backwards compatibility mandatory: old logs without ids must keep parsing.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25: Pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small, Low risk). Ran six automated review stages. Corrected AC4 `tests/fixtures.py` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, AC7 `REFERENCE.md` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`. Plan complete — item ready for implementation.
data.title: Add per-turn correlation id to all structured log lines

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want `Stream finished` lines to say explicitly
when an upstream reported no token usage, so "no data" is distinguishable from
"zero tokens" and sessions with unknown context are countable rather than
invisible.

## Why

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` only appends `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
when the upstream response carries a `usage` object:

```
if isinstance(usage, dict): ... parts.append(f"tokens=...")
```

When a provider (or an aborted/errored stream) omits usage, the line silently
has no `tokens=` field. In the 2026-10-23/24 window this left 3 of the 26
local-using sessions with no context size at all (their `Stream finished`
lines carry no tokens), so any analysis of "context at fallback" for them
degrades to n/a with no way to tell why at the log level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a terminal stream has no reportable usage, the `Stream finished`
  line carries an explicit marker (e.g. `tokens=missing` or `usage=none`),
  emitted from the same code path in `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`.
- AC2: The marker never overrides real usage — a present `usage` object still
  logs `tokens=p/c/t` exactly as today (no format change for the populated
  case).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill counts the new marker:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  stream-finished event, and `aggregation.py`/`reporting.py` report a
  "streams without usage" count (window-level, and per-session where the
  context-at-fallback table is rendered) instead of silently emitting n/a.
- AC4: `reporting.py` limitation text in the affected sections names the
  marker as the cause of missing context figures.
- AC5: Tests: a fixture line with `tokens=missing` in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, plus tests in
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` proving (a) missing-usage streams are counted
  and excluded from token totals, and (b) populated lines are unchanged.
  Proxy-side test for the emit path in `proxy/tests/` (whichever suite covers
  `router_helpers` stream-finish logging).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (any code doing
  `tokens=` regex matches must not treat `missing` as a number).
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker and its meaning.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — emit path for the `tokens=missing` marker (AC1, AC2, AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parses the marker onto the stream-finished event (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — "streams without usage" count (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — count in report + limitation text (AC3, AC4).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixture line with `tokens=missing` (AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — analyser tests for the marker (AC5).
- `proxy/tests/test_stream_entry_name_logging.py` — proxy-side tests for the emit path (AC5).
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` — consumer audit: `tokens=` regex must not treat `missing` as a number (AC6).
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — documents the marker and its meaning (AC7).

## Notes

- Small, contained change; the risk is consumers that regex
  `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)` — those simply won't match the marker, which is
  the desired behaviour, but each should be verified rather than assumed.
data.title: Emit explicit tokens=missing marker when upstream reports no usage

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip vocabulary is renamed to
  `provider_budget_exhausted`, everywhere it is emitted: the
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), the `reason=` text in the
  `Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=...` log lines, the
  `fallback_reason = ...` assignments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (~9028, ~10515), **and the diagnostics attempt `status` values**
  `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"` (~9018, ~9038,
  ~10505, ~10525) -> `status="provider_budget_exhausted"` /
  `status="provider_budget_exhausted_waited"`. Producer decision
  (2026-10-25): *full rename everywhere* — no `rate_limited*` literal may
  remain in **newly emitted** code paths, tests, or current documentation.
  The analysis-skill legacy mapping (AC3) and `REFERENCE.md` deliberately
  retain the old spelling as a *historical* name (exactly as
  `warm_cache_bypass` is retained next to `context_too_large`).
- AC2: Internal decisions/behaviour are unchanged: the affinity/reserve/wait
  logic and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the rename must not alter
  decisions — it is a string rename only). `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` is updated
  to key on the new status (`frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})`,
  provider.py ~4181); `status_code=429` in the diagnostic attempt entries
  stays as-is (a numeric HTTP code, not the reason vocabulary); the
  reason-keyed budget-evidence gate `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")`
  (~669) switches to the new prefix.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s. Paths verified at plan
  time: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` (legend at
  ~line 545) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (~lines 478, 544, 731).
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; every test that asserts the old

  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py`, `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`,

  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`.
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and

  With the full rename the attempt-`status` assertions also move:

- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:

  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Historical artifacts are

- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.
- AC9: Current documentation examples that show the reason *or* attempt-status

## Notes

- **Deferral cleared:** renaming alone does not fix mis-attribution, it only

## Implementation notes (verified at plan time)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` carries all four reason variants —

- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py:80` is a comment describing field

- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` renders raw log lines — display sanity check only.
- Test-function names carrying the old vocabulary (rename with the change;

- Test-first order: (1) parser normalisation tests (old + new spellings) in

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — all four `BudgetDecision.reason` values and their log lines.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `fallback_reason` assignments (~9028, ~10515), reason-keyed evidence gate (~669), `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` (~4181), docstrings.

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser/analysis assertions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- ~~OPEN QUESTION 1~~ **ANSWERED (producer/Map, 2026-10-25): "full rename

  Q: Does the rename cover only the emitted *reason* value, or also the

  Alternative: rename the status vocabulary too (`provider_budget_exhausted`

  the status assertions in `test_provider_budget.py` (~1187),
  `test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` (~75, ~169),
  `test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357), `test_quota_state.py` (~360) and the
  `status:` examples in `proxy/README.md` / `proxy/docs/routing.md` /

- Q: `AC5` listed `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and

data.title: Rename budget-skip reason rate_limited to provider_budget_exhausted

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want local prompt-eval (prefill) throughput increased so that
large cold prompts become cheap enough to serve locally, unlocking real local
utilisation instead of diverting work to paid remote providers.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This item must only be executed once we have had a successful night of local
LLM consumption, meaning >60% GPU utilisation across a full night.** Until
local actually carries sustained work (>60% local busy), tuning prefill
throughput is premature: there is no sustained workload to measure against and
no evidence that prefill latency — rather than routing policy — is the binding
constraint. Verify the gate with the `proxy-usage-analysis` report's
`## Local model utilization` section for a night window (e.g. 22:00-07:00):
it must show busy >= 60%. Record that evidence in a comment on this item
before starting work; if the gate is not met, leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Prompt-eval speed (llama-server eval timing, Qwen3, fast bucket): median
  **90.7 tok/s**, p90 316.7, p10 24.9 (532 samples, 24h window
  2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52).
- Per-stream prefill (dispatch -> first byte): p50 4.4s, p90 35.3s, max 73.7s.
- `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 90` — a slow prefill can be cancelled, and
  prior incidents show cancelled prefills re-dispatching identical prompts
  (the prefill-thrash cooldown exists because of this).
- The prefill-ETA admission guard refused **478** local admissions in the
  window on projected prefill cost, and only **34** requests were admitted by
  the idle override despite local being idle 89.8% of the time.
- Current llama-server launch flags (Qwen3 child):
  `--ctx-size 262144 --parallel 2 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 1024
  --cache-ram 40960 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0
  --swa-checkpoints 32 --no-mmap -ngl 80 --threads 8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment on this item records the measured >60% GPU utilisation
  for a full night, taken from the usage-analysis report, before any change is
  made. Work does not start without it.
- AC1: A measured baseline is captured first: prompt-eval tok/s distribution
  (p10/p50/p90), prefill phase duration, prefill-ETA admission refusals, and
  prefill-thrash events over a fixed window, all from the
  `proxy-usage-analysis` artifacts.
- AC2: Prefill throughput is improved by tuning the llama-server launch
  configuration (candidates: `--ubatch-size` 1024 -> 2048/4096, `--batch-size`,
  `--mlock`, thread count, SWA/checkpoint settings) and/or the prefill-related
  proxy knobs (`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`, the ETA guard budget). Each
  changed value is justified by measurement, not by guesswork.
- AC3: The optimisation is measured with the same method as AC1 and the
  before/after comparison is recorded on this item, including any effect on
  decode speed (no regression to decode tok/s median) and on stability
  (`slot_save failed`, prefill cancellations, HTTP 400/503 rates).
- AC4: If a knob change affects the prefill-ETA guard's behaviour, the guard's
  configuration and documentation are updated together, and the
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / ETA interactions are documented.
- AC5: The usage-analysis skill is updated if new or changed log evidence is
  needed to measure the improvement
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{llama_log_parser.py,log_parser.py,
  reporting.py}`, `REFERENCE.md`), and any other log-consuming script that
  reads llama-server eval timings or prefill evidence is audited
  (`proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_lease_verification.py`).
- AC6: Launch-flag changes are documented in `models.ini` / start-proxy
  documentation so the settings are reproducible, and any start-proxy script
  or test asserting the flags is updated.
- AC7: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- This item is downstream of routing policy: raising local demand (thresholds,
  serve-first admission) comes first, otherwise there is nothing to optimise
  for. Keep the gate.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate increasing local ctx-size) and the
  slot-geometry experiment (1 slot vs 2) — decide ctx/slot geometry before
  micro-tuning batch sizes, since the two interact.

## Plan (2026-10-25)

Decomposed into nine children. Every change-making child is dependency-blocked
on the **gate child** (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ, *Verify sustained local utilisation gate*) and on the gated geometry experiment
(LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN), so nothing starts before AC0 is satisfied. This item
itself depends on the gate child and therefore renders as `blocked`.

| # | Child | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verify sustained local utilisation gate (LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ) | AC0 | — |
| 2 | Baseline prefill measurement capture (LP-0MVNBJWRH006V9Y6) | AC1 | 1 |
| 3 | 40-80k prefill benchmark capability (LP-0MVNBJX3G008IBTB) | AC2 (measurement validity) | 1, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 4 | Measurement evidence and log-consumer audit (LP-0MVNBJXF9002DJAZ) | AC5 | 1, 2 |
| 5 | Launch-flag A/B: ubatch and batch size (LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD) | AC2 | 1, 2, 3, LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN |
| 6 | Launch-flag A/B: threads and SWA checkpoints (LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51) | AC2 | 1, 5 |
| 7 | ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review (LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J) | AC2 (proxy knobs), AC4 | 1, 2, 5, 6 |
| 8 | Post-change verification: latency and stability (LP-0MVNBJYPM004UV56) | AC3, AC7 | 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 |
| 9 | Document launch flags and reproducibility (LP-0MVNBJZ100020UN0) | AC6 | 1, 5, 6 |

Sequence: gate -> baseline + harness capability (test-first) -> launch-flag
A/B -> guard review -> post-change verification + docs. Each child is a
vertical slice carrying its own tests, config/docs change and measurement
record.

Vertical-slice decision: the change is deliberately **not** phased into
separate "code" and "docs" phases; each A/B child lands flag + test + comment
together, because an undocumented or untested flag change is not deliverable.

**Effort/risk (this plan):** Medium (`recommended 51.22 h`, range 33.3-76.0 h)
/ **Medium** (score 10). Estimate source: `effort-and-risk` skill with this
plan's per-child WBS; it replaces the `0.00 h` autoplan placeholder recorded
earlier.

**Gate status at planning time:** NOT met (busy 2.2 % for the night
2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00; 10.2 % over the 24 h daily report).
Children that change configuration must not start until AC0 is satisfied.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Answered by repository / work-item evidence (non-interactive planning run):

- Q: "Is the AC0 gate (>60 % local busy for a full night) met?" - Answer
  (evidence: `proxy-usage-analysis` CLI + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`):
  **No.** 2.2 % busy for 2026-10-23 22:00 -> 2026-10-24 07:00 (719 s of
  32 400 s, 27 streams, prefill 336 slot-s, decode 383 slot-s); 10.2 % for the
  24 h window 2026-10-23 10:52 -> 2026-10-24 10:52. Source: CLI run recorded in
  the pre-check comment (`/tmp/wl-gate-check`).
- Q: "Has micro-batch tuning already been attempted, and with what result?"

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and
  `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to
  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors
  (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.


---

## Plan (2026-10-25, /skill:plan)

Sequenced features in dependency order (execution order for `wl next`):

1. **Gate: verify 60% local busy night** (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG) — parent AC0 evidence; blocks the arms.
2. **Geometry A/B protocol and reporter** (LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP) — `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` (protocol, window, metrics, pre-registered gate), `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` + fixture tests, `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` apply/verify helper. Test-first; can start while the gate is unmet.
3. **Arm A capture: 2 slots 131K** (LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K) — blocked by 1+2.
4. **Arm B run: 1 slot 262K** (LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY) — blocked by 3; warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp, cold unchanged, band non-collapsed.
5. **Arm comparison and geometry decision** (LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY) — blocked by 4; applies the pre-registered gate, records verdict + follow-on item.
6. **Propagate geometry decision to docs** (LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7) — blocked by 5; models.ini / config.yaml comments, usage-analysis REFERENCE, log-consumer audit.
7. **Suite green and geometry assertions** (LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP) — blocked by 6; `/skill:test` green + slot/ctx alignment assertions.

Reuse: env plumbing already exists (`LLAMA_PARALLEL`, `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` in start-llama.sh; `session_slot_pool_size` drives it); per-slot clamp/band logic is in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with existing unit coverage; usage-analysis report already emits busy/prefill/decode metrics. Precedent harness: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`.

Pre-registered decision-gate defaults (proposal — confirm at implement time unless overridden by the producer): adopt **1 x 262K** when, relative to Arm A, (a) turns served locally does not decrease, (b) `context_too_large` + `large_context_bypass` diverts fall by >= 50 %, (c) p90 dispatch→first-byte does not worsen by > 30 %, (d) local busy % does not regress by > 10 points; otherwise keep 2 slots (or choose mode-dependent with the recorded numbers).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-25)

- Q: "Arm B's warm threshold: raise to the new per-slot clamp (~258K) or keep ~120K?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: raise the economic ceiling ratio so warm = clamp (258,048), cold unchanged (38,000), band non-collapsed (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). Rationale: leaving it at 120K means the extra slot context is never routed to, defeating the arm. Final confirmation delegated to implement time unless the producer overrides.
- Q: "What makes 1 x 262K 'win'?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed pre-registered gate above (mirrors the ubatch A/B precedent LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD). Confirmation delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Arm window length?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: one full night (22:00 → 06:00 local, >= 8 h), Arm A then Arm B on the same weekday type, identical length for both. Delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Write the protocol while the gate is unmet?" Answer (plan): yes — child 2 has no dependency on the busy gate (desk work), so implementation can begin immediately and the gate evidence decides when the arms may run.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25Z (plan session herdr-1792903336-2608898-6919): superseded the placeholder auto-skip verdict (XS/0.00 h) with a genuine estimate (Medium effort/Medium risk); ran full /skill:plan decomposition. Created 7 children (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG gate, LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP protocol+reporter, LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K Arm A, LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY Arm B, LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY comparison+decision, LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7 docs propagation, LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP suite green) in test-first order with dependency edges C3<-C1,C2 / C4<-C3 / C5<-C4 / C6<-C5 / C7<-C6. Ran the six automated review stages (trace bullets added; Key Files validated), AC coverage review proceeded (7/7), stage advanced to plan_complete. Effort/risk re-estimated (Medium, WBS from children).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to record real prompt/completion token usage
for local streams, so that (a) local cache-credit and context accounting can
work from measured data and (b) the usage-analysis report can measure actual
local prompt sizes instead of showing them as unknown.

## Why (evidence)

Local `Stream finished` lines **never carry `tokens=`**:

- 225 of 225 local `Stream finished` lines in the window 2026-10-23 10:52 ->
  2026-10-24 10:52 have no token field;
- **0** lines with `tokens=` exist in the entire log archive (2026-10-17 ->
  2026-10-24) for `provider=local`.

Consequences:

1. **The usage-based cache-credit path is dead for local.** In
   `proxy/router.py` (~line 566) `update_cached_ratio()` and
   `record_prompt_prefix()` are only called when the response carries a usage
   block with `prompt_tokens > 0`. Because local never reports usage, the
   expected-reuse credit (`LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV`) can never be earned from
   measured tokens. Credit today comes only from the slot-snapshot seeding
   path (655 `slot_save success` events in the archive), so a session whose
   first local dispatch did not produce a snapshot stays permanently "cold"
   (ratio 0.00) and is then bypassed by the 38K cold-cache rule on every later
   turn.
2. **The report cannot measure local context.** In the window, 3 of the 26
   sessions that used local had no context size at all, and the per-model
   token table attributes local tokens only via sessions whose *initial*
   provider was local — not via actual local streams.
3. Two current analysis outputs are therefore guesses rather than
   measurements: per-session local prompt sizes, and the cache-state
   attribution used in the skip-reason explanation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Local `Stream finished` lines include `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
  with values taken from llama-server's reported usage (its response/`usage`
  payload or `/slots` accounting — whichever is authoritative), for
  non-streaming and streaming paths.
- AC2: `update_cached_ratio()` and `record_prompt_prefix()` therefore fire for
  local streams with measured values, so the expected-reuse credit is earned
  from data rather than only from a saved slot snapshot. Verify with a test
  that a 30K local turn followed by a 40K total / 10K new turn routes local
  (the intended cold-cap semantics: the cap applies to NEW, uncached tokens).
- AC3: A regression test proves the sequential-caching case explicitly:
  turn 1 total 30K -> local; turn 2 total 40K with ~10K new -> still local
  (new tokens below the 38K cold cap). This is the behaviour the design
  intends and it currently cannot be demonstrated from the logs.
- AC4: The usage-analysis skill consumes the new data:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` and
  `aggregation.py` attribute tokens to local streams, `reporting.py` reports
  real local prompt sizes and a "streams without usage" count, and the
  limitation text that currently explains missing local context is updated.
- AC5: Other log consumers relying on `tokens=` are audited:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`.
- AC6: Tests: skill fixtures/tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` plus proxy-side tests for the emit
  path.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents local token reporting and the cold-cap
  semantics (cap applies to new/uncached tokens; total context is bounded
  separately by the warm cap).
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Notes

- Complements LP-0MVMBM6N400541EH (`tokens=missing` marker): that item makes
  absence explicit; this item fixes the root cause (local usage is never
  reported at all, so the marker would fire on every local stream).
- Do not change routing thresholds here — this is measurement plumbing, and it
  is a prerequisite for measuring any later routing change honestly.

## Goal

Evaluate (with measurements, go/no-go) whether widening the **per-session KV snapshot pool** (`session_slot_pool_size` 2 → 4, snapshots under `session_slot_save_path/slot_<id>.bin`) raises local prefix reuse for the small/medium working set — as the recommended alternative to adding live llama slots, which would shrink per-slot context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots) and exclude the long-context sessions that dominate this workload.

## Why

- Measured prefix reuse is poor: aggregate 26.1 %, median **15.6 %** for prompts >20k tokens (227 prompts), 28 fully cold; 27 distinct sessions cycled through a 2-slot pool in ~5.4 h.
- More live slots buy *residency*, not throughput (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills), and cost per-slot address space for a long-context workload.
- The snapshot mechanism already exists (per-session save/restore, `session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds: 0.0015`, capped at `session_slot_max_timeout_seconds: 60`, pool capped by `session_slot_pool_size: 2`) but is degraded under load (`session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`, circuit-breaker cooldown). Restore cost estimate: ~50k tokens ≈ 75 s → capped 60 s, so the mechanism currently helps only the <40k band.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Benchmark:** measure save/restore latency (and disk footprint) per prompt-size band (10k / 25k / 40k / 60k+) on the production GPU host, including under load (another session streaming), against the 0.0015 s/token timeout model.
- **AC2 — Go/no-go with evidence:** with `session_slot_pool_size: 4` in a replay/bake-off on the 2026-10-24 thrash window (or equivalent fixture), report the reuse uplift (baseline 15.6 % median for >20k prompts) and the restore-success rate (skip_when_busy / cooldown exclusions).
- **AC3 — If go:** ship the config change plus retention/eviction semantics for 4 snapshots (pool eviction policy, disk cap, failure cooldowns unchanged) and any report/observability fields (restore-hit rate per session, snapshot pool occupancy) so the proxy-usage-analysis report can monitor the effect.
- **AC4 — If no-go:** record the measured blockers (latency, skip rate, restore failures) as a comment on this item so the decision is reproducible.
- **AC5 — No change to live slot count or per-slot ctx in this item** (that remains the separate 3-slot "fast" profile discussion).

## Tests

Bake-off harness replaying fixture logs + real save/restore micro-benchmark on the host; unit tests for pool-size > 2 retention semantics; report-schema tests for the new fields.

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (slot-churn / tenancy investigation, option 3a of the recommendation).
- This is an evaluation/deliberation item, not a mandate to change configuration.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWJIBIE0012HDD** – Slot-count benchmark: find optimal session_slot_pool_size for Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MPOL5S7W007GRWB** – Include router model in slot save/restore requests (completed)
- **LP-0MU03AL730000B5W** – Slot counts: default and fast -> 1 slot, cheap -> 3 slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mvn1iqtf0037wtg, 20k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+140 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: 10k, 50k, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+134 more)

## Goal

Execute the **24 h post-deploy verification of AC4** for
`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` (resident-prefix admission + session tenancy) and report
whether scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` cancellations fell by
**>= 90 %** relative to that window's own re-anchored baseline.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-26T00:51Z.** That is the provable lower bound
(creation time + 24 h). The real instant is the **later** of
`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`'s deploy and `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy, **+ 24 h** —
retitle this item with that concrete ISO-8601 UTC instant when both have
shipped. Do not run before it.

## Why

AC4 of `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` requires this verification, but it cannot be done
inside the implementation session: it needs a full 24 h production soak after
the scheduler change and after the cold-prefill budget change
(`LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`, 25k tokens + deadline 90→110 s) are both deployed.
Keeping it here prevents the implementing session from measuring its own work
too early and calling it verified.

## Preconditions (check before running)

1. `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` is deployed to the proxy (resident-prefix gate, tenancy
   bound, live-prefix pricing, AC5 log fields present).
2. `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed (25k cold budget, 110 s deadline).
3. The proxy has been up continuously for the whole 24 h window — a restart
   inside the window invalidates the run (in-memory residency state resets).

## Measurement window

- 24 h, ending on a `05:00 UTC` boundary so it aligns with the daily
  `proxy-usage-analysis` cron report; record the exact start/end instants
  (ISO-8601 UTC) in the result comment.
- Re-anchor the baseline **to that same window** (post-budget-change), not the
  2026-10-24 figures (160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted prefill tokens), which
  become historical reference only.

## Procedure

1. Base counts: `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events in the window, and total
   wasted prefill tokens.
2. Classify each event as *scheduling-attributed* when either
   (a) `reuse_ratio` logged at admission was below
   `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or
   (b) `slot_owner_session` changed between admission and the deadline event
   (prefix evicted by another session).
   Everything else is a genuine GPU-speed miss and is out of scope.
3. Run the usage analysis for the window:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
   (see `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` for options) and extract the
   resident-vs-evicted reuse split and slot-owner churn (AC5 signals).
4. Compare the scheduling-attributed residual against the re-anchored baseline
   and state the percentage reduction explicitly.

## Verdict criteria

- **PASS:** scheduling-attributed cancellations down **>= 90 %** vs the
  re-anchored baseline, with no `local_lease_active` refusal window exceeding
  the 180 s watchdog bound (AC6).
- **FAIL / follow-up:** either threshold missed → record the measured numbers,
  create a `discovered-from` item for the regression (with the offending log
  extract), and do not mark this item complete.

## Deliverable

A result comment on this item containing: window start/end, precondition
attestation (deploy times, proxy uptime), absolute event/token counts, the
scheduling-attributed split with the classifier applied, the percentage
reduction vs baseline, and the PASS/FAIL verdict. Then close with
`<WIP-id>: <summary>`.

## Links

- Verification target: `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` (AC4, AC5, AC6).
- Budget change whose deploy starts the clock: `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`.
- Historical baseline: `docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`,
  the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 proxy/llama-server logs under
  `/var/log/llama-proxy`.

## Deploy terms at arming — re-armed 2026-10-25T11:25Z by `LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P`

The operator confirmed (2026-10-25) that **dev code runs live on this server**:
no `dev`→`main` release is required to deploy, so the deploy instant is the
proxy (re)start that picked the code up.

- **`LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`** — live from **2026-10-25T11:21:22Z** (uvicorn pid
  2858324). Code identity at that instant: local `dev` = `67b38266`
  (= `origin/dev` `c30b6d76` + the concurrent `LP-0MVN4LCED00661MX`
  commits `90fb019e` / merge `67b38266`). Record the tree with
  `git log -1 --format=%H` **from the checkout the running proxy was started
  from** when you open the verification window — the checkout is shared with
  other agents, so the tip can move without a restart. The ladder is verifiably emitting: the first
  decisions after the restart log
  `routing_resident_prefix … n_past_actual=none … reuse_ratio=none …
  residency_source=non_resident` (the corrected form — see
  `LP-0MVNPZY22008B536`), and the usage report renders the
  `## Residency-aware admission` section from live data.
- **`LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`** — its work is also on `dev` (25k budget, deadline
  120 s) and therefore live from the same restart instant, **but the item is
  still in progress**: more of its code may land.
- **Earliest run instant: 2026-10-26T11:22Z** = max(11:21:22Z, 11:21:22Z) + 24 h.
- **Re-arm rule (binding):** any further restart of dev code before the window
  starts moves the clock — retitle to `latest_restart + 24 h` before running.
  A restart *inside* the window invalidates the run (in-memory residency/lease
  state resets), so confirm continuous uptime ≥ 24 h
  (`ps -o lstart -p <uvicorn pid>`) as the first precondition. Note the proxy
  has restarted twice on 2026-10-25 (11:01:57Z for the epic's landing, 11:21:22Z
  for the observability fix), so neither instant is usable as the window start.

## Pinned measurement window (fill in before running)

- `start: <ISO-8601 UTC>` / `end: <ISO-8601 UTC>` — 24 h, ending on a
  `05:00 UTC` boundary (aligns with the daily report cron).
- Proxy must have been up for the whole window; any restart resets the
  in-memory residency state and invalidates the run.

## Baseline re-anchoring query for that window

```bash
# 1. Absolute counts in the window (scheduling-attributed split below).
grep -c "prefill_deadline_exceeded" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*      # window-scoped
# 2. Residue model, re-anchored: capture the window, then replay it through
#    the residency-aware ladder (same oracle as the 2026-10-24 baseline).
python3 proxy/scripts/capture_prefill_thrash_window.py \
  --start "<start>" --end "<end>" --out /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl
python3 proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py x \
  --window-fixture /tmp/ac4_window.jsonl        # expects 0 over-budget cold admissions
```

## `proxy-usage-analysis` invocation

```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
  --start "<start>" --end "<end>" --output-dir ~/proxy-usage-reports/ac4
```

Read the `## Residency-aware admission` section (resident-vs-evicted reuse
split, per-session slot-owner churn, evictions by reason) and the
`residency_decisions` / `residency_resident_admits` / `residency_evicted_denials`
/ `residency_tenant_limit_denials` / `local_evictions` counters in the JSON
summary. **This is also the staged-rollout observability check for
`LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P`:** the section and those counters must appear in the first
post-deploy report cycle — if they are absent, the ladder is not emitting
(`routing_resident_prefix`) and that is a finding, not a pass.

## Scheduling-attributed classifier

An event counts as **scheduling-attributed** when either:

- (a) the `reuse_ratio` logged at admission
  (`routing_resident_prefix … reuse_ratio=<f|none>`) was below
  `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or
- (b) the `slot_owner_session` logged at admission differs from the owner at
  the deadline event (the prefix was evicted by another session).

Everything else is a genuine GPU-speed miss and is out of scope.

## Goal

Prove the shipped change with the parent's AC4 measurement: run the 24 h post-deploy window through `proxy-usage-analysis` and record the evidence (deadline-event rate vs the 2026-10-24 baseline, eviction counter for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens, client-visible 503/retry rate) on the parent item.

## Context

Parent AC4: scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h ≈ 30/h), the AC7 eviction counter zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s/retries. The window starts at the `POST /admin/reload-config`/restart that makes the new config live (per the intake note, a config reload is sufficient) — record that timestamp on this item before starting the measurement.

## Scope

**In:** post-deploy 24 h measurement, evidence recorded as a work-item comment, verdict + follow-up items.

**Out:** further code changes (any regression found becomes its own work item), the release/`dev`→`main` promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window defined and recorded.** The reload/restart timestamp that made the new config live is recorded before the window starts; the analysed window is ≥24 h after it.
- **AC2 — Regression evidence (parent AC4):** over the 24 h window post-deploy, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h), the AC7 eviction counter is zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s / retries. Each of the four checks is recorded with its measured number and pass/fail verdict; the ≤10 % check is the primary gate (≈3 events/h or fewer).
- **AC3 — Eviction counter (parent AC4/AC7).** `local_evictions_after_acceptance` is reported with its per-reason breakdown; pass requires **0** for within-budget prompts, and any non-zero count is recorded as a defect signal with a follow-up work item.
- **AC4 — Waste and client impact (parent AC4).** Wasted prefill tokens are compared with the ~780k baseline, and 503/retry counts are compared with the pre-change window; "no increase" is asserted with the actual numbers.
- **AC5 — Evidence + follow-ups.** Results are recorded as one structured comment on this item (numbers, window bounds, command used) and referenced from the parent; every failed check has a linked follow-up work item.
- **AC6 — Rollback decision.** If a check fails, the comment states which rollback knob(s) were applied (budget `0` / deadline `90` / percentile-min `32768` / safety fraction `0.0`) and why, or records an explicit decision to keep the change.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`

## Implementation sketch

1. Note the reload timestamp; wait the full window (no early peeking that could bias the decision).
2. Run `analyze_proxy_usage.py --json` over the window plus the baseline window; capture both summaries.
3. Tabulate the four checks and record pass/fail with numbers.
4. File follow-ups for any failure; record the rollback decision.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by "Prefill budget/deadline config knobs + ordering assertion".
- Blocked by "Enforce cold-prefill budget on all admission paths".
- Blocked by "Post-acceptance eviction ERROR events and counter".
- Blocked by "Usage report eviction metrics and triage rule".

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a repeatable measurement protocol plus an arm-comparison
reporter, so both geometry arms are measured over identical windows with
identical metrics and tooling (parent AC1, AC3).

- Precedent: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py` (A/B harness that archives raw JSON under `benchmark-results/` and pre-registers a numeric gate).

- Per-slot context is derived, never configured directly: `--ctx-size / --parallel`, clamped by `effective_per_slot_threshold()` (`ctx_size // slots - 4096`), i.e. 2 slots -> 126,976 and 1 slot -> 258,048.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` records the arm definitions (A = 2 x 131,072 current; B = 1 x 262,144), the identical window length and the preferred same-weekday night span, the per-arm metric list, the exact commands, the raw-data archive naming convention, and the **pre-registered numeric decision gate written before any measurement**; a protocol summary (window length, metric list, decision gate) is also recorded on the parent LP-0MVMHNUXW0061FGN (parent AC1: 'defined and written on this item').

# Pin start-proxy.sh shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision with a pytest test

## Problem statement

`start-proxy.sh --restart` decides whether to preserve a warm llama-server by
comparing the `config_sha256` recorded in `.llama_server_signature.json` with a
freshly computed `merged_config_sha256` of `proxy/config.yaml`; on a match it
preserves ("Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)."),
otherwise it kills and restarts llama-server. That shell branch is currently
the **only** untested consumer of the merged-config signature: the sole
coverage lives in `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, which
LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 deletes (mode-era harness). The Python tests cover the hash
helper and the signature writer (`proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`,
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`), not the shell decision that acts on
them — so a regression there (e.g. comparing the wrong path, ignoring the flag)
would go unnoticed and would either kill a warm llama-server on every restart
or silently preserve a stale one.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — the warm KV/prompt cache must survive a proxy-only
  restart, and a genuine local-backend change must restart llama-server.
- **Future implementation agents** — need the shell branch pinned so changes to
  `start-proxy.sh` restart handling fail loudly in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Unchanged config preserves llama-server.** A pytest test runs a
  sandboxed copy of `start-proxy.sh --foreground --restart` whose signature
  file matches `merged_config_sha256(proxy/config.yaml, proxy/config.yaml)` and
  asserts the "Preserving running llama-server" line is emitted and the fake
  `pkill` log contains **no** `llama-server` kill.
- **AC2 — Changed config restarts llama-server.** With the sandbox config
  edited after the signature was written (merged hash changes), the preserving
  line is absent and the fake `pkill` log shows a `llama-server` kill.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe signatures.** Missing, empty or corrupt signature /
  unreadable hash → conservative restart (never an unearned preserve), asserted
  behaviourally.
- **AC4 — Explicit override still wins.** `--keep-llama-server` forces
  preservation even when the signature mismatches (flag beats hash).
- **AC5 — Sandbox isolation.** The test copies the script into a temp dir with
  stubbed `pkill`/`fuser`/`ss`/`netstat`, an isolated `$HOME`, an ephemeral port
  and a fake interpreter intercepting the final `exec uvicorn`; it never
  touches the live proxy, llama-server, TTS or ports 8000/8080/8081, and never
  issues a blanket kill. It is collected by the default pytest suite (unlike
  the bare `tests/*.sh` harnesses).
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.**
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `start-proxy.sh`: this is coverage for the existing
  contract. A defect found while writing it becomes a separate work item.
- Reuse the established sandbox pattern in
  `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` (fake `python3` recording argv,
  stubbed process/port probes) rather than inventing a new harness.
- The signature schema is written by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
  (`_write_llama_server_signature`: `mode`, `model`, `parallel`, `router_mode`,
  `config_sha256`); fixtures must match it.
- UK English.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (being deleted by LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29) holds
  the only behavioural assertions for this branch; after deletion the branch has
  none.
- `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only that harness and
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` asserts the flag is *documented*
  (`test_start_proxy_help_documents_keep_llama_server`) and pins the Python hash
  helper — not the shell preserve/restart decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_signature.py` — new pytest test (name
  indicative).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` — sandbox pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — script under test (read-only).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `merged_config_sha256` fixture hash.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — signature schema reference.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — deletes the stale mode-era harness; this item
  replaces the one piece of live coverage that deletion removes.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H**, **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — duplicate items closed
  in favour of LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (producer decision B).
- **LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW** — restart signature hashes the merged config.
- **LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN** — preserve-the-warm-llama-server design.

## Observed behaviour (2026-10-25, UTC)

Session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (`/skill:intake RISE-0MVLHZW7B003XEHV`) was pinned to local routing by its client (`X-Local-Preference: local-only`). The local admission guard refused it:

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true
              priority=medium session=herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152
11:57:09,999  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=false  (same session)
```

Both refusals were answered with **HTTP 429 and `error: "All providers exhausted"`**:

- direct/lease path: `provider.py:10450` → `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`code: local_admission_reject`)
- contention-queue path: `provider.py:10785` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`error: "Local admission refused"`)

Remote providers were *available* throughout (`opencode-go` at 62 % effective headroom), so "All providers exhausted" is factually wrong, and the two paths disagree on the message for the same condition. The client (which retries on 429) backed off seven times and then reported the error as non-retryable; the user-visible symptom was "Error: 429 \"All providers exhausted\"".

## Goal

A local-only admission refusal is a *capacity/intent* outcome, not a chain exhaustion: it must be reported with one stable, distinguishable contract on every path, and "All providers exhausted" must be reserved for genuine chain exhaustion.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both local-only refusal paths (direct/lease `provider.py:10450`, contention-queue `provider.py:10785`) return the same shape: HTTP 429, `Retry-After`, `X-Local-Route: refused`, the `X-Local-Admission*` headers, and a body whose `error` text does **not** contain "All providers exhausted".
2. The body carries a stable `code` distinct from `all_exhausted`, `outside_time_window` and `all_slots_exhausted` (e.g. `local_admission_refused`), and the human-readable `detail` states that the request was pinned local-only and the local guard refused it.
3. Genuine chain exhaustion is unchanged: `code: all_exhausted` / `outside_time_window` / `all_slots_exhausted` and the existing prose remain byte-compatible for older clients.
4. `prefer-local` fallthrough behaviour is unchanged: a guard refusal with `prefer-local` still routes to the next provider and never returns the refusal response.
5. `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the refusal codes, the "local-only" semantics and the client-side action (compact/retry/allow remote).
6. Tests: unit coverage for both refusal paths asserting status, `code`, `error` text and headers; a regression test asserting a real chain exhaustion still returns the exhaustion codes; a test asserting a local-only refusal *while remotes are available* never uses the exhaustion prose.
data.title: Local-only admission refusal must not report 'All providers exhausted'

## Observed behaviour (2026-10-25, UTC)

Diagnosing session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (429 "All providers exhausted") required grepping `proxy.log` for chain-exhaustion events that never existed: the refusal leaves **no trace at all** in the proxy log, while a *false* fallback line is emitted for it.

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true  session=herdr-1792897705-…
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard_direct_fallback provider=local-qwen3 … → routing to next provider
              ← nothing was routed: provider.py:10447 returns the 429 for local-only
```

Consequences:

- `provider.py:10432` logs `… → routing to next provider` *before* the local-only branch returns the 429 at `provider.py:10450`, so the log states the opposite of what happened.
- Neither the direct path (`:10450`) nor the contention-queue refusal (`:10785`) logs the refusal itself, so a 429 handed to a client is invisible in `proxy.log` — the only trace is the guard's `decision=reject` line, which is indistinguishable from a `prefer-local` refusal that fell through and succeeded remotely.
- Operators cannot count or alert on this failure class, and log-based diagnosis mis-attributes it to chain exhaustion.

## Goal

Every local-only admission refusal is attributable from the proxy log alone, and no log line claims routing that did not happen.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line is emitted only when the request actually falls through to the next provider; for a local-only refusal it is either not emitted or clearly qualified as a refusal (no "routing to next provider" wording).
2. Each local-only refusal emits exactly one INFO line with stable `key=value` fields, e.g. `local_only_refusal session=… provider=… reason=… new_tokens=… budget_tokens=… eta_prefill_seconds=… budget_seconds=… priority=… route=refused`, for **both** the direct/lease and contention-queue paths.
3. The refusal is countable from the log by a single stable token (`local_only_refusal`), and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (or the logging docs) documents that token so runbooks and the `proxy-log-debug` skill can grep it.
4. Tests: a test asserting the refusal log line is emitted for a local-only refusal on each path; a test asserting the misleading "→ routing to next provider" line is **not** emitted for a refused local-only request; a test asserting a `prefer-local` fallthrough still emits the fallback line.
5. Verification note: the 2026-10-25 11:57:09 case is reproducible in a test and the log output is shown in the work item.
data.title: Local-only admission refusal is invisible in proxy logs and logs a false fallback line

## Goal

As an operator I need a persisted history of GPU compute activity, so that questions like "how busy has the GPU been since the last restart?" can be answered from direct measurement rather than inferred from proxy request logs.

## Context

Investigating GPU utilisation for a window (2026-10-25, after asking "what has local llm and GPU usage been like since the last restart?") established that **no usable GPU utilisation measurement currently exists**:

- `gpu_busy_percent` is **pinned at 100% regardless of actual GPU state** on this hardware (Strix Halo / Radeon 8050S / gfx1151). Documented in `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py:43-48` and config comment at `proxy/config.yaml:974`, and re-confirmed LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP. Sample taken during this investigation: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 while `power1_average` = 44 W (GPU idle).
- `power1_average` on this host is the discriminating signal: **~44-54 W idle vs ~115 W computing**. The threshold is already configured: `llama_gpu_wedge_power_low_threshold_watts: 90`.
- The proxy health loop reads GPU busy + power (see `_read_gpu_busy_percent`, `_gpu_busy_percent_sysfs`, `_gpu_busy_percent_rocm_smi` in `proxy/proxy/backends/llama.py`) but **never logs the readings**: `grep -icE "gpu_busy|gpu_power|gpu_wedge" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` returns 0. There is therefore **no history to reconstruct**.
- No external collector is running: Prometheus / node-exporter / Grafana are all absent (`systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` shows none). `proxy/benchmarks/prometheus_snapshot.sh` collects GPU metrics only on demand, as a manual snapshot.
- Consequence: the only utilisation figure available is the proxy-usage-analysis report's `local_busy.busy_pct` (20.2% for that window), which measures "a local stream was in flight", **not** GPU compute — its `dispatch -> finish` interval includes queue wait before llama.cpp accepts the task and client streaming time at the end.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A sampler persists **timestamped samples on a configurable interval** (default 10 s) containing at minimum: `power1_average` (W), `gpu_busy_percent`, per-slot busy/idle state plus in-flight task count from `GET /slots`, and GPU memory in use (VRAM + GTT).
2. Samples are written to a **durable, rotating store separate from `proxy.log`**, with configurable retention; the store schema and retention policy are documented.
3. A query/CLI path reports, for an arbitrary time window: **computing-time percentage** = fraction of samples where `power >= compute threshold` **and** at least one slot is busy; plus idle %, mean/max power (W), and peak concurrent slots.
4. The reported computing-time percentage is **independent of `proxy.log`** — it must be reproducible with the proxy log absent, proving it is a direct measurement rather than an inference.
5. `gpu_busy_percent` is recorded for completeness but is **explicitly labelled unreliable on gfx1151 and never used** to compute the utilisation figure (a regression test asserts this).
6. Sample **gaps are explicit**: sampler downtime or missing samples are reported as `unknown` and are never silently counted as idle.
7. The idle-vs-compute power threshold is **calibrated and documented for this host** (idle ~44-54 W, compute ~115 W, threshold 90 W), with a note on how to re-measure it.
8. Unit tests cover: interval selection, threshold/percentage arithmetic, sample parsing, retention/rotation and gap handling; an integration test runs the query path over a fixture sample stream. Each test asserts a meaningful behaviour, not just non-None.
9. Full suite green via `/skill:test`; docs updated (where the sampler runs, how to query it, retention, and how to interpret computing-time % vs the report's `busy_pct`).

## Notes

- Deliberately scoped to **measurement**, not to changing the proxy-usage-analysis report. The report's existing `busy_pct` remains valid as a local-path occupancy metric; this item supplies the missing true GPU figure.
- Follow-up option (not in scope here): feed the sampler's output into the usage report as a "True GPU utilisation" section.
- Related: LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP (established that `gpu_busy_percent` is pinned and power is the discriminating signal).
data.title: Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation history

## Problem

A child work item whose acceptance criteria are execution-dependent ("All new tests run through the test skill and collect cleanly", "full suite passes") can never be marked `met` by the audit's child screening, because the child Phase-1 screen and Phase-2 deep-analysis prompts do not carry the green-run evidence block (or the execution-dependent AC rules) that the parent prompts receive.

Observed 2026-10-25 auditing `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` (resident-prefix admission / session tenancy epic): child `LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H` was scored `partial` with the evidence "All seven manifest files are well-formed pytest modules … but actual run-through of /skill:test and clean collection with the rest of proxy/tests is an execution result not verifiable under this read-only audit (no pytest run performed)". That single `partial` is the last thing keeping the epic's own audit at `Ready to close: No` — every parent AC is `met`/`adjusted` and code quality is clean, while the green full-suite run at the same HEAD (`3c9b8e34`, `3c5413ac`) exists and is consumed for the parent's AC9.

## Impact

A parent with any execution-dependent child AC is permanently un-closable through the audit, and each re-audit re-demotes the child out of `in_review` — churning delivered work (10 children were demoted during this session; the demotion also produced two stale-state children that had been `Ready to close: Yes`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — evidence reaches child screens:** the child Phase-1 screen and child Phase-2 deep prompts receive the same verified green-run evidence block (and the execution-dependent AC guidance) the parent prompt receives, when such evidence exists at the audited HEAD.
- **AC2 — no false `partial`:** a child AC that is execution-dependent is marked `met` when the cached full-suite run at HEAD is green at `scope == full`, and `partial` (with the existing diagnostic) only when no such evidence exists.
- **AC3 — regression test:** a test asserts the child prompt includes the green-run evidence text when the cache is green, and that the resulting verdict path does not degrade to `partial` for that AC.
- **AC4 — no scope widening:** the parent/child AC rules, models and JSON contract are otherwise unchanged; child screens still never execute the suite themselves.

## Goal

As an operator I need the Prometheus monitoring stack to be **deployable from the
repository, reachable only over the tailnet, and honest about GPU utilisation on
this hardware**, so that GPU/local-model history can be queried directly instead
of being inferred from proxy request logs.

## Context

On 2026-10-25 a "what has local LLM usage and GPU busy state looked like over the
last 2 hours" question could only be answered from the proxy-usage-analysis
report's `local_busy` figures (dispatch -> finish wall clock), because **no GPU
utilisation history existed**: Prometheus, node_exporter and Grafana were all
absent from the host, despite LP-0MQR554O60033BGF being marked completed/done.

The stack was then installed and started by hand (host-first, systemd user
units): Prometheus 3.15.1, node_exporter 1.12.1, and a 10 s sysfs sampler feeding
node_exporter's textfile collector. Three problems surfaced that belong in the
repository, and they are the children of this item:

1. `monitoring/prometheus.yml` **could not start at all** — `rule_files` repeated
   the `monitoring/` prefix although Prometheus resolves those paths relative to
   the config file's own directory (LP-0MVO8DO7100309LH).
2. The GPU series the repository still advertises are either unpublishable
   (`rocm_vram_*`, because `amd/rocm-exporter` has no release artifacts) or
   actively misleading (`gpu_busy_percent` is pinned at 100 % on this Strix Halo
   APU, LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP) — so two of the five alert-rule groups can never
   fire (LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48).
3. The deployment procedure, the tailnet-only exposure posture and the new
   systemd units exist only on this host, not in the repository (LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `promtool check config monitoring/prometheus.yml` succeeds from the repository
   root and the config can start Prometheus with no manual edits.
2. Every alert-rule group in `monitoring/` is backed by a series that is actually
   published by a running exporter, verified by querying Prometheus for each
   series named in a rule expression.
3. `docs/systemd/` and `monitoring/README.md` describe the exact units, binds and
   exposure boundary that are running on the host, including how GPU metrics are
   obtained on this hardware.
4. No alert rule or documented dashboard refers to `gpu_busy_percent` as a
   measure of GPU utilisation without stating that it is pinned on this APU.

## Notes

- Children are independent; none blocks another.
- Related, deliberately not duplicated: LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W (GPU telemetry
  sampler) — Prometheus + node_exporter now provide the persisted history that
  item's AC2 asked for; the residual gap is noted there.
data.title: Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus with honest GPU utilisation
